Its normalization is $-c^2=g(U,U)=m^2c^4g(W,W)$, hence $m=1/(c\sqrt{-g(W,W)})$ and the second formula in (2) follows. Conversely, on $C=0$, contraction of $K^a{}_b$ with $p_a$ gives $p_aK^a{}_b=\mu^2p_b$ because $p_aS^{ac}=-C^c=0$. Multiplying by $W^b$ yields $g(p,W)=-1$, so the normalized formula has $m=-g(p,U)/c^2=1/(c\sqrt{-g(W,W)})$ and satisfies the first formula in (2).

On the open region stated in the theorem, the inverse $K^{-1}$ and the positive square root $\sqrt{-g(W,W)}$ depend smoothly on the state coordinates. The smooth Lorentzian background, curvature and metric-selected connection [F2, F6] make the coordinate form of $z'=U$, (1) a smooth, hence locally Lipschitz, vector field. [F5] gives unique local solutions. For constraint preservation, set $\lambda:=c/\sqrt{-g(W,W)}$, so $KU=\lambda p$ throughout this open region. The product rule [F1] gives
$$D_\tau C^a=p^a g(p,U)+\mu^2U^a+S^{ab}f_b=p^a(g(p,U)+\lambda).$$
Moreover, $p_aK^a{}_bU^b=\mu^2g(p,U)-C^bf_b=\lambda g(p,p)=-\lambda\mu^2$, so $\mu^2(g(p,U)+\lambda)=C^bf_b$. Therefore
$$D_\tau C^a=\frac{p^a f_b}{\mu^2}C^b.$$
